A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SkewScore research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, algorithms, and appendices A–J are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix J report original synthetic causal-discovery experiments, runtime and robustness results, and 62.6% accuracy on the Tübingen cause-effect pairs.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix J retain original synthetic experiments and the Tübingen result. Results retained from v1 remain original empirical results of this work.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same score statistic, iterative sink selection, and conditional-independence graph recovery. The suggested near-zero-score diagnostic and possible FCI extension are additional discussion, without a changed discovery algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate bivariate, triangular-confounded, and multivariate HSNMs, Gumbel noise, additive-noise models, multivariate confounding, and Tübingen pairs. The new distribution calculations in Appendix A are theoretical examples, not additional empirical coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding experiments: HECI, LOCI, HOST, DiffAN, DAGMA, and NoTears retain their roles, and VarSort remains in the sample-size comparison. Table 8 repeats Figure 3's comparator set; FCI is suggested but not evaluated.

E3.justification: The stated sample sizes, score-estimation network, optimization settings, CI subsampling, metrics, and appendix evaluation designs are retained. Removing two data-generation disclosures does not establish that the underlying protocol changed.

E4.justification: The Gumbel-noise robustness test, additive-noise comparison, sample-size sensitivity, runtime study, and multivariate-confounding analysis are retained. No new empirical ablation, robustness test, or case study is added.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 runs for pairwise experiments and 10 for multivariate experiments, retain the same uncertainty displays, and introduce no new seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Table 8 claims to reproduce Figure 3 but contains conflicting values. For bivariate Sig-abs/Student's t, HECI is tabulated at 64% versus 81% plotted; for the confounded counterpart, SkewScore is tabulated at 100% versus 96% plotted. Figure 3, Tables 1–7, and the Tübingen result are unchanged. These are changed numerical reports, without documented reruns or setting changes.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds a conditional-symmetry proof and explicit Gumbel and Gamma score-skewness derivations. Appendix D adds a piecewise-smooth extension of Fact 2 and an exponential-distribution counterexample. These extend supporting mathematics while the central identification theorems and confounding guarantee remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: skewness-based identification of HSNMs, SkewScore without exogenous-noise extraction, and theoretical robustness in a triangular confounding model.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly warns that multivariate DAG recovery can create spurious edges under latent confounding. Appendix J identifies discrete data and violations of symmetric heteroscedastic assumptions as challenges on Tübingen. Section 4.2 and Appendix C also discuss assumption diagnostics and dependence on the odd test function.

D1.justification: Section 6 removes v1's specification of linear confounder effects with slopes sampled from (-2, -0.5) union (0.5, 2), together with the statement that data are standardized. These details are not restored elsewhere. Network, optimizer, and hardware disclosures remain.

R1.justification: Section 5 newly connects a possible confounding-aware extension to FCI and Partial Ancestral Graph recovery. The related-work survey and cited-work set otherwise remain stable; consolidating the duplicate Mityagin reference is bibliographic cleanup.

P1.justification: Most prose and the section sequence are retained. Local revisions expand and rename Appendix A, rewrite the multivariate genericity discussion, clarify supporting explanations, and update author information and acknowledgements.

P2.justification: The document adopts ICLR formatting throughout, changing fonts, margins, headings, headers, and the placement and sizing of displays. Algorithm 1 and Figures 3–4 are repositioned, Figure 6's labels are expanded, and Table 8 adds a grouped, color-highlighted display of the pairwise results.

improvement.justification: The added mathematical explanations and applicability limits are useful, but v2 weakens empirical reporting by introducing unexplained Table 8/Figure 3 contradictions and removing confounder-generation and standardization details. These losses in consistency and reproducibility outweigh the limited clarification benefits. The core method and most evidence remain intact, so the deterioration is limited.
